Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, Planning Commission Members will be participating via
teleconference.

- Commission meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city/agendas and available for
viewing thereafter. Commission meetings are recorded for minutes preparation purposes.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
894 8557 9649 Passcode: 511168. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in option from
a phone line.)

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol Corea, Administrative  Assistant  at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Commission for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”
button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After
you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
public, will be considered by the Commission and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting, may join by visiting http://www.zoom.com/join
and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 894 8557 9649 Passcode: 511168.

- If using a tablet or phone, download the Zoom app and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 894 8557
9649 Passcode: 511168.

Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you
would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agendas.

MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, MAY 3, 2021

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order by CHAIR EDLER at 7:00 p.m. Pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20, this
  meeting was held via teleconference.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR EDLER led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioner’s Present:  Edler, Scott, Medawar, Schachter, Yoo

  Commissioner’s Absent:  Carman, Zigrang

  Staff Member’s Present:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development and Public
  Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES, APRIL 5, 2021.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF APRIL 5, 2021.

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the Planning
  Commission will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by title only.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210102; ADDRESS: 5 SWEETGRASS LANE;
  APPLICANT: JURE SESTICH; A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination
  (NC-210103) for conversion of 852 sq. ft. second floor storage/attic to livable area.

  Planning Manager Naughton provided a presentation summarizing the staff report for Planning
  Application No. PA-210102. The attic area is currently being used as storage and the applicant is
  proposing to convert the space into livable area. To meet the required head room area, a thirty-one
  foot shed dormer along the west elevation and a twelve foot shed dormer on the east elevation will
  need to be added. This project is being presented to ensure that the addition of these dormers will
  not impact any views in this neighborhood. A silhouette was erected and stayed in place for more
  than 14 days; no correspondence was received regarding this project adversely impacting any views,
  however there was one letter of support submitted for the project by one of the adjacent neighbors,
  provided as Attachment D.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff recommends approval of Planning Application No. PA-
  210102, approving a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-210103) for conversion of 852
  sq. ft. second floor storage/attic to livable area, subject to the conditions outlined in the staff report.

  CHAIR EDLER opened the meeting for public comment.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, MAY 3, 2021
  1
   (No comments)

  CHAIR EDLER closed the meeting for public comment.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210102 AS PRESENTED, SUBJECT TO
  THE CONDITIONS OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT.

  AYES: Edler, Scott, Medawar, Schachter, Yoo
  NOES:
  ABSENT: Carman, Zigrang
  ABSTAIN:

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning
  Application No. 210102, a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-210103) for conversion
  of 852 sq. ft. second floor storage/attic to livable area at property address, 5 Sweetgrass Lane.
  There will be a 20-day appeal period where any member of the public may appeal this decision to
  the City Council.

  B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-200373 - RHEMC FENCE REGULATIONS
  MODIFICATIONS STUDY SESSION

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that these fence regulations were presented to the Planning
  Commission in the Fall of 2020. Per the direction of the Planning Commission, staff has included
  more photos with examples of various fences as well as refined some of the recommendations.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that currently all residential fences in front yards are limited to
  twenty-four inches in height, except for the Horse Overlay District. There are many examples where
  twenty-four inches is not sufficient. Staff is proposing that there be a maximum allowable fence
  height of forty-two inches. Examples were provided to show the fences that could complement
  various architectural styles. (RHEMC Section 17.06.350)

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that he is in favor of this as it provides homeowners flexibility
  on how they can landscape their front yards.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT expressed his concern with this proposal since three-rail fences are not
  architecturally appropriate in some neighborhoods and it is not a feature that is necessary to make
  these lots usable.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that three-rail fences would not be the only option, this would
  also apply to hedges, stucco walls, and solid wood fences.

  Director Wahba stated that with a forty-two inch fence (as opposed to a twenty-four inch fence), it
  can be more of a statement and can help keep a pet or child from getting out into the street. Forty-
  two inch fence height is standard in most cities.

  Planning Manager Naughton added that this would extend to garden features that are over twenty-
  four inches in height. Staff is trying to find a compromise to maintain the openness but also adapt
  to the desires of the community to improve the front of their properties.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that there are properties that do not have large front yards; this may
  change the character of the neighborhood and make some homes look closed in.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff can come back with options where allowances could
  be made for walls, fences, landscaping features that are over twenty-four inches based on certain
  circumstances. Staff would also like to get away from contemplating variances for properties that
  need to exceed the twenty-four inches.

  CHAIR EDLER expressed his concern with allowing this; in some neighborhoods, having some
  homes with fences and some without, could have a negative look. There should be a solution where
  staff can approve these over the counter, however, and when the proposed fence is completely out
  of character with the neighborhood, staff can bring it to the Planning Commission for review.

  COMMISSIONER YOO inquired on how many requests for fences higher than twenty-four inches
  have been received by staff. Planning Manager Naughton stated that in the past two years, there
  have been about a dozen requests for fences above twenty-four inches.

  Director Wahba stated that staff could include some criteria if someone is proposing to do a solid

  2
   fence, it will need to be setback and integrated to the landscaping.

  Planning Manager Naughton continued with RHEMC Section 17.06.370.A - solid fences, hedges
  and walls on street facing side yard need to meet the same setbacks as the primary dwelling. If the
  fencing is open (permitting 90% light and air to pass through it) such fencing can be placed on the
  side property line. Staff is recommending that the setback be a minimum of two feet or eighteen
  inches for the purpose of providing landscaping between the fence and the sidewalk, where a
  public sidewalk is present. Additional changes are proposed for private streets and open fences.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made comments on the examples shown, but there were no comments
  opposing staffs recommended changes.

  Planning Manager Naughton continued with RHEMC Section 17.06.370.B, Fences, hedges, and
  walls - side and rear yard setbacks, grade differences. Staff is recommending that the 42” be
  specific to retaining walls and that property owners be allowed a six-foot high solid fence or wall on
  the side property line regardless of the grade separation.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that this would allow a way for the City to be able to regulate
  these fences, since currently, a building permit is not required.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT provided an example of the wall between his property and his neighbor’s
  property, and stated that he is in full support of the forty-two inch retaining wall and six foot high
  solid fence or wall. COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR concurred.

  Director Wahba stated that the combination fence with grade differences needs to go away; you
  could have a six-foot retaining wall, which is typically offset from the property line a minimum of
  two feet. Planning Manager Naughton added that in the residential district retaining walls are
  restricted to five feet in height.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that in the code, these sections require a horizontal separation
  to be equal to the highest fence or wall. Retaining walls are restricted to a maximum of five feet in
  height and if a property owner proposes to put a fence on top of the retaining wall, the code prohibits
  it. In addition, if a property owner proposed to do a series of retaining walls or a fence in combination
  with their retaining wall, it would need to be setback at least six feet horizontally. Per the building
  code, a forty-two inch high safety railing is required plus the six foot separation before a six foot
  high fence could be allowed.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff is recommending that the horizontal separation be
  reduced to two feet and that within the two feet there be landscaping provided between the walls
  or wall and fence. Regarding the required safety rail, staff is requesting direction from the Planning
  Commission whether to allow a solid or partially open safety rail.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that he is in favor of the two feet horizontal separation; however, if
  there is a six-foot fence, which is two feet from the retaining wall and there is landscaping between
  them, then a safety rail is not necessary. Director Wahba stated that in this case, it would not be
  required since it is not a usable area.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked if this applies to side yards where there is limited space or
  common space with your neighbor. Planning Manager Naughton stated that it does apply.

  A brief discussion ensued.

  Planning Manager Naughton continued with RHEMC Section 17.40.40 – parcels of land used for
  off-street parking or vehicle sales. There are not many lots where this affects typical planning
  review and stated that staff recommends that this section be simplified to allow for an administrative
  avenue for allowing alternative fence/wall heights for non-residential uses that are adjacent to
  residential properties, such as the CalWater facility at the corner of Montecillo Drive and Encanto
  Drive and the overflow parking area at the Jack Kramer Club.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that for the CalWater project there is a great case for a Variance since
  it is a noisy facility in the middle of a residential neighborhood. In the case of the Jack Kramer Club,
  he does not think it is a good idea to put a six-foot fence on top of the berm. The church parking
  lot has never had anything in terms of fencing.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the intention of this section is to protect light shining into
  residents and reduce the impacts for a property being used for parking.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that these three properties are different and does think this should
  come to the Planning Commission so that those impacted have an opportunity to be heard.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, MAY 3, 2021
  3
   Planning Manager Naughton stated that these applications could be handled similar to
  administrative entitlements for residential districts, which require that public notices be sent to a
  five-hundred foot radius. There would be a comment period and an appeal period.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that he would be in favor of this.

  Planning Manager Naughton continued with RHEMC Section 17.66.100 – Minor Deviations. There
  are two minor deviations in relation to wall and fence heights. Staff is recommending that Minor
  Deviation #9 be eliminated and that Minor Deviation #4, be noted that a special use permit is
  required for the exception of fenced recreational enclosures.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that he is in support of these.

  Planning Manager stated that staff will come back with draft language including the feedback that
  was received from the Planning Commission.

  8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210119; ADDRESS: 2-C PENINSULA CENTER;
  APPLICANT: MARIO OCHOA, GWA ARCHITECTURE; A request for approval of a
  Conditional Use Permit (CUP-210120) for a new restaurant use at the Peninsula Shopping
  Center.

  Associate Planner Thom presented Planning Application No. PA-210119 summarizing the staff
  report. A CUP is required in order to allow a restaurant since the space was previously a different
  use.

  Associate Planner Thom stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open the
  public hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues, close the public hearing; and adopt
  Resolution No. PA-210119 approving the project.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that there was a comment from the public regarding grilling in
  the restaurant. Associate Planner Thom stated that she was informed that there is minor grilling and
  they will have the appropriate range hood equipment in place.

  Planning Manager Naughton added that the correspondence pointed to the Habit Grill that is in the
  same shopping center. However, they have specific allowances for charbroiling which produces
  different odors from the business which is different from a flat top grill. This Jersey Mike’s does not
  have charbroiling.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  Mario Ochoa, GWA Architecture, stated that they have a flat top grill and stated that it is not
  constantly being used. The grill is used per order and there are grease filters throughout the hood
  that will clean out the smoke that is going through the exhaust fan, so the odor will be minimal.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210119

  AYES: Edler, Scott, Medawar, Schachter, Yoo
  NOES:
  ABSENT: Carman, Zigrang
  ABSTAIN:

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning
  Application No. 210119, adopting Resolution No. PA-210119 approving a Conditional Use Permit
  (CUP-210120) for a new restaurant use at the Peninsula Shopping Center. There will be a 20-day
  appeal period where any member of the public may appeal this decision to the City Council.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, MAY 3, 2021
  4
   9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT inquired about the project at 9 Lantana. Director Wahba stated that they are
  close and are waiting for agency referral sign-off at LA County Building & Safety.

  NONE

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS – APRIL 13, 2021

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 11A – 11B

  CHAIR EDLER adjourned the meeting at 8:43 p.m. to the next Planning Commission meeting on
